answer: A seat votes only while an opal that already votes locks jade behind it, and the river records every lock. The k-th seat one opal backs needs 100k jade locked, so a lone honest newcomer costs its opal 100 jade. An operator vouching for his own clones from one opal locks 100+200+…+100k, about 50k² jade. Twenty clones tie up 21,000 jade, and the 20th alone costs 2,000. Spreading them across unrelated opals means paying each one to risk jade that the river forfeits if its seat is proven a clone.
